The '''Sorcerers of Tund''' were a largely reclusive, secretive ancient order of [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark siders]] from [[Tund/Legends|Tund]], a remote, shadowy [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Centrality/Legends|Centrality]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] and were notable for their [[Tundan robes|concealing outfits]]. The Sorcerers were highly skilled in deception, [[Mind trick/Legends|illusions]], and shapeshifting. They rarely ventured off Tund, and were known to be driven mad by their explorations of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].

==History==
[[File:Sorcerer_of_Tund_JATM.jpg|thumb|left|A Sorcerer of Tund displaying Force abilities.]]
The Sorcerers of Tund were established on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tund/Legends|Tund]] following the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]],<ref name="TEA" /> believed have been during the [[Third Great Schism]] of [[4250 BBY]].<ref name="FoundingNote" /> They were originally composed of [[Kissai heretics]] who were exiled from<ref name="Web Enhancement" /> [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]].<ref name="TEA" /> This pure-blooded Sith society – spoken of in whispers throughout much of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] – combined science, ontology, and magic. Convinced by their Rakatan interactions that all sentients are [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]], the Sorcerers of Tund proclaimed the omnipresence of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] ("the Unity") that illuminated the deception of dualities and multiplicity.<ref name="Web Enhancement" />

The early Jedi viewed the sorcerers as merely another<ref name="Web Enhancement" /> [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]<ref name="The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force" /> Force sect, much like the [[Jal Shey]] or [[Zeison Sha]]. But following the Restoration&mdash;and reign of terror by [[Karnak Tetsu]], who led the sorcerers in the years following the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]&mdash;the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] viewed the Sorcerers' hermetica as a heresy.<ref name="Web Enhancement" /> The [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] tried to recruit the Sorcerers, but were unsuccessful.<ref name="The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force" /> The sorcerers were reticent in accepting outlanders, believing that only [[Sith (species)/Legends|true Sith]] can grasp their truth. However, they welcomed the few remaining [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] and [[Kissai]], descended from outcasts much like themselves.<ref name="Web Enhancement" />

[[File:AdlerRotyAd-HoloNetNewsVol531-45.png|thumb|right|100px|An advert for the show of Adler Roty, who claimed to be a Sorcerer of Tund.]]
During the waning years of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], numerous crises forced the Jedi to abandon their surveillance of the Sorcerers. [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] did not see any potential for recruitment in the ranks of the Sorcerers, believing that the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]] could contain [[Tund/Legends|Tund]].<ref name="The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force" />

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], [[Adler Roty]] claimed to be a Sorcerer of Tund.<ref name="Adler Ad">{{HoloNetNewsAd|url=meta/img/ads/600_3.gif|text=Adler Roty}}</ref> The last known disciple of the group was [[Rokur Gepta]], a [[Croke]] who joined the group, learned all their secrets of power, invented a few of his own, and when he felt that there was nothing more to learn, [[Destruction of Tund|killed the others and all other life on the planet]] with his [[electromagnetic torpedo]].<ref name="LCFO">''[[Lando Calrissian and the Flamewind of Oseon]]''</ref> Gepta would repeatedly come into conflict with [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] during the early years of the gambler's career,<ref name="LCA">''[[Star Wars: The Lando Calrissian Adventures]]''</ref> eventually dying at his hands, thus seemingly eradicating the order.<ref name="LCST">''[[Lando Calrissian and the Starcave of ThonBoka]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
When he envisioned "[[Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties]]" in [[2001]], [[Abel G. Peña]] intended the Sorcerers of Tund to be the product of a peaceful [[Second Great Schism]] in ~[[10,000 BBY]].<ref name="JCF">{{JCFCite|url=posts/24255327|board=Literature|thread=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties|user=[[Abel G. Peña|Halagad_Ventor]]|PTtime=2006-06-29|quote=...I never updated the Sorcerers of Tund section of Evil Never Dies (which originally had them as a group of Jedi schismatics of an intellectually rather than violently motivated Second Great Schism, placed around 10,000 BBY)...|archiveurl=https://boards.theforce.net/threads/evil-never-dies-the-sith-dynasties.24202765/page-9#post-24255327}}</ref>

The ''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]'' mistakenly states that all Sorcerers of Tund are members of the [[Croke]] [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref>
